status: Written before execution. New fluid-only experiment after user explicitly selected actual Navier-Stokes stress; no molecular stress runs performed.
equations: du/dt=P(u cross curl u)+nu Laplacian u, div u=0; constant density, periodic [0,2pi)^3; positive nu; no forcing, subgrid model, hyperviscosity, particle feedback or mass changes.
starts: Common analytic finite Fourier-mode Kida-Pelz and 3D Taylor-Green fields on every grid. All dimensional quantities are model units; no real-water parameter mapping.
stress: Kida nu=0.02,0.005,0.001 through t=2 on N=32,48,64,96; N=128 refinements of low-viscosity and high-viscosity endpoints. Taylor-Green nu=0.01,0.001 through t=4 on N=32,64,96.
perturbations: Kida nu=0.005, fixed low-mode divergence-free perturbations orthogonal to baseline in kinetic-energy inner product, adjusted to preserve initial total energy. Four seeds at epsilon=0.001 on N=48; seed 1 at eps=1e-6,0.001,0.01 on N=64 and96. These are flow perturbations, not molecules or mass substitutions.
method: Strict componentwise |k|<N/3 Fourier dealiasing, pressure projection, float64/complex128, classical explicit RK4, dt<=0.01 and adaptive advective CFL target0.35/diffusive dt limit. Checkpoints every0.5 (Kida) or1 (TG), diagnostics every0.1.
time_controls: Half timestep on Kida N64 nu0.005 and0.001, plus N64 nu0.005 epsilon0.001 seed1. Initial analytic tests, exact decaying ABC and advected ABC tests precede ensemble.
screens: Predeclared descriptive screens, not rigorous error bounds: tail enstrophy fraction<1%, abs energy budget residual<0.1%, divergence RMS<1e-9, finite fields, CFL<=0.5; spatial normalized velocity L2 difference<1% and Wmax difference<5% at matching times. Time controls: velocity L2<0.2%, Wmax<1%. A failed screen marks an unresolved interval, not equation failure. Continue after spectral failure to expose artifacts; stop on nonfinite values or gross energy/step failure.
measurements: Energy, dissipation, enstrophy, stretching minus viscous loss, maximum vorticity, peak location, energy spectra, cutoff enstrophy, whole-field error, finite-time perturbation amplification, difference participation fraction. Same seeds and initial modes across grids. No asymptotic Lyapunov or singularity claims from finite windows.
limits: Finite Fourier Galerkin systems remain regular and cannot prove continuum blowup. Increasing high-grid vorticity alone is insufficient. Resolution and time controls may disagree. Old project starts/checkpoints and molecular results remain separate. Runs incomplete or omitted for resources must be reported explicitly.
